question: The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 (Rural) of India allows ranking of the households under 'Others' category based on their status on _______ deprivation parameters.
solution:
The correct answer is __**seven**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 (Rural) of India ranks households under the 'Others' category based on their status on **seven** deprivation parameters.
 
• The SECC 2011 was conducted to identify households living below the poverty line and to gather socio-economic data for effective policy-making.
 
• The deprivation parameters include criteria such as households with only one room with kucha walls and roof, no adult member between ages 16 to 59, female-headed households with no adult male member aged 16 to 59, among others.
 
• This ranking helps in the identification of the most vulnerable and disadvantaged households for targeted welfare schemes and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The SECC 2011 data is crucial for the implementation of various government schemes aimed at poverty alleviation and social welfare.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on the socio-economic status of households, including details on education, employment, assets, and housing conditions.
 
• The SECC 2011 was a collaborative effort between the Ministry of Rural Development, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation, and the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• The data collected through SECC 2011 has been used to create a database of eligible beneficiaries for various government programs such as the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), National Food Security Act (NFSA), and others.
